conversation.Statement: Hello, this is Agent Smith from the Internal Revenue Service. Am I speaking with Mr. Patel?
Yes, this is Raj Patel. May I ask what this is regarding?
Mr. Patel, according to our records, there are discrepancies in your recent tax filings. It appears you owe a substantial amount in unpaid federal taxes.
I'm sorry, I don't understand. I just started working here a year ago and I thought my taxes were automatically deducted.
Unfortunately, that is not the case. The IRS has found that you failed to declare certain overseas income, which is a serious violation.
I wasn't aware of that. I didn't mean to do anything wrong. What happens now?
Mr. Patel, if this matter is not resolved immediately, a warrant for your arrest will be issued. In addition, your professional license could be suspended and your bank accounts frozen.
Arrest? My license? This sounds very serious... I can't lose my job. Is there something I can do?
The IRS is offering you a one-time opportunity to settle this outside of court. But you must act now to avoid legal consequences.
Okay, I want to fix this. What do I need to do?
You will need to make an immediate payment of $2,492. This must be completed today to pause any enforcement action. We only accept electronic or prepaid payment for urgent cases like yours.
I don't have that much cash on me. What kind of payment do you need?
You can purchase Target or Best Buy gift cards in the total amount. Once you have the cards, you'll provide me with the codes on the back.
Um, gift cards? Is that really how the IRS collects payments?
Due to fraud prevention, high-priority cases are processed through secured prepaid transactions. You must stay on the line while you purchase the cards so I can verify every step.
Alright, I'm going to the store now. Should I get $2,492 all in one card?
No, split the amount across multiple cards, no more than $500 per card. Call me back when you have them, and do not discuss this matter with anyone at the store for your own privacy.
I understand. I'll call you once I have the cards. Please, don't take legal action yet.
